subject: geography

moments.title: Millennium Development Goals
moments.body: 189 nations adopt the Millennium Declaration in September 2000. Eight Millennium Development Goals follow, targeting 2015: halve extreme poverty, achieve universal primary education, reduce child mortality, combat HIV/AIDS/malaria. Largely framed as goals for LICs.
moments.takeaway: The MDGs were the first global development framework with measurable targets and a deadline. Their reach was contested but their political effect was real.

moments.title: Sustainable Development Goals
moments.body: September 2015: 17 SDGs with 169 targets agreed, to be met by 2030. Universal (apply to all countries, not just LICs), integrate environment and development, and address inequalities within countries. Goal 13 is climate action; Goal 5 is gender equality; Goal 10 is reducing inequalities.
moments.takeaway: The SDGs were paired with the Paris Climate Agreement (December 2015) — the most ambitious year for multilateral environmental policy.

moments.title: Halfway point
moments.body: September 2023: SDG Summit reports that of around 140 targets evaluated, only 12% are on track. COVID-19, conflict (Ukraine, Sudan, Gaza) and the cost-of-living crisis have set back many indicators.
moments.takeaway: The 2030 deadline is unlikely to be met for most goals at current trajectory.

now.title: Development under pressure
now.body: Global poverty (Goal 1) had been falling rapidly pre-pandemic; COVID-19 was the first reversal in decades. Climate (13) and biodiversity (14, 15) indicators are worsening. Health (3) progress on under-5 mortality is real but slowing. The framework remains the main global development reference.
now.open_questions: Are 17 goals too many to prioritise? The Copenhagen Consensus argues for triage; the UN line is that integration across goals is the point.

reflection: Global development targets shape national policy even without enforcement. The MDGs and SDGs are case studies in how internationally agreed numbers become national plans — and how external shocks can derail them all at once.
